comment: What the S3's FIRMWARE costs: the shipped image (esp32s3,server,float-f32 — lp-fw/fw-esp32s3's own default feature set, the bytes the M4-walk XIAO ESP32-S3 Plus is flashed with) direct-loaded on lp-emu:esp32s3:t1 and read from its FIRST heartbeat triple. ⚠️ That triple is ELICITED, not idle-emitted, exactly as on the classic and NOT as on the C6: `esp32_memory_stats` (M6 P04b) runs on a project load/unload/stop-all or a client `runtime_status`, never on the five-second server heartbeat — a periodic printer would flood the very USB-Serial-JTAG link the transport runs on. The gate asks for it with lp-emu/lp-emu-validate/walks/s3-stop-all.script — the same bytes on the same trigger line as lp-emu-esp32s3/tests/boot_idle.rs — and stops on the first `[JIT] used=` line. `measured` is this tree, and is the ratchet. Regenerate with `just heap-budget-baseline-chips-s3`; see docs/heap-budget-gate.md, "The second source".
sample: the FIRST heartbeat triple, elicited by one `stopAllProjects` on `[INIT] I/O task spawned` +1 ms, with the host attached from power-on; the run ends on the first `[JIT] used=`
boot_shape: DIRECT LOAD, no flash chip — the other two chips' shape and for their reason (the bootloader adds wall clock and nothing to the answer; rom_up_boot.rs holds the two paths byte-equal at the application's entry). ⚠️ With no flash there is no partition table, so this firmware logs `no lpfs partition in the flashed table … using memory FS` and runs on the memory FS. That is a DIFFERENT ALLOCATOR LOAD from a flashed board's, and it is why these figures are a ratchet on this tree rather than a prediction of what a board prints. For scale: the same image booted ROM-up off the merged 8 MiB chip, with its lpfs mounted, reports `[MEM] free=229188 used=16568 largest_free=229175` (M6 P06) — ~1.4 KB more used, all of it the filesystem. Compare like with like, and never a figure here with a figure from there.
structural_zeros: Two claims this chip's idle boot makes that are NOT figures and so are not ratcheted: `retry_saves=0` on the `[MEM]` line, and the whole `[JIT] used=0 peak=0 cap=0 spans=0 peak_spans=0 allocs=0 frees=0 fails=0 largest_free=0` line — an idle boot on this chip JITs nothing (M6 P04b). heap-budget-check.sh asserts both as constants and fails with that reason, because a number appearing there is a finding about what the image DOES rather than about what it costs, and a record-only gate would never see it.
stack_band_note: MEASURED ON ONE HOST (this desk — M2 Max, aarch64-apple-darwin). The runner's figure does not exist yet: the `Emulator ESP32-S3 (x64)` job lands with this phase and its first green run is where that number comes from. The band is the measurement ±500 B rounded outward — the C6's rule (DD45's measured host-to-host spread was 128 B there, and the classic's two hosts later agreed to the byte) and not a fitted number. ⚠️ Until a second host has reported, this band is one host's claim about a layout-dependent figure: the image a CI runner builds is not this host's binary (the classic's `host_band` measured 500 B of drift at one commit), and a tick landing on a different instruction of a differently laid-out image has a different deepest point.
silicon_reference_note: There is none, and that is the honest state: NO S3 SILICON HAS BEEN READ. P09 owns the desk sitting that produces one. The C6's and the classic's rows carry a `silicon_reference` printed beside every run so the gap cannot widen unseen; this chip's will be added by the phase that measures it, and until then nothing here is a claim about hardware.
